assumptions: The test named is the test the experiment will run, on independent observations.
The effect size is the true one: a pilot or literature estimate carries its own uncertainty into the answer.
The t tests assume normal errors (equal variances unless the unequal-n form is chosen); the proportion tests use the normal approximation (arcsine h for pwr, R's power.prop.test otherwise).
limits: A sample size is a minimum for the stated power, not a guarantee: attrition, dropout and failed samples are not included.
No multiple-testing adjustment is made; pass the per-test significance level the analysis will use.
Count data (RNA-seq) is calculate_rnaseq_power's question, not this one's.
bio.jane/contract.question: How many replicates does a planned test need to detect an effect, or what power, detectable effect or significance level does a fixed design give?

description: Power and sample size for a planned experiment: how many replicates a test needs to detect an effect, or what power, detectable effect or significance level a design that is already fixed gives. Leave ONE quantity out with `solve_for` and it is solved; everything else is given. Thirteen tests in two families: Cohen's standardized effect sizes (pwr 1.3-0: t one/two-sample/paired and unequal n, one and two proportions by arcsine h, normal mean, correlation, chi-square w, one-way ANOVA f, linear-model f²) and raw units (R's power.t.test from a difference and SD, power.prop.test from two proportions, power.anova.test from variances). Every number is R's, reproduced: the solved value is uniroot's root at R's tolerance, and an unreachable target is refused with R's own message. Returns the power curve around the answer and the R call that reproduces it.

N.description: total observations across every cell. Only applies when test is chisq.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alternative.description: two-sided, or the direction a one-sided test looks in (the raw-unit t and proportion tests take only two.sided or one.sided). Only applies when test is t or t_unequal or two_proportions or two_proportions_unequal or one_proportion or normal_mean or correlation or t_raw or proportions_raw.

between_var.description: variance of the group means. Only applies when test is anova_raw.

df.description: degrees of freedom of the chi-square test: (cells − 1) for goodness of fit, (rows − 1)(columns − 1) for independence. Only applies when test is chisq.

difference.description: δ, the true difference in means, in the measurement's units. Only applies when test is t_raw.

effect.description: the standardized effect: Cohen's d for t and normal-mean tests, h for proportions, r for correlation, w for chi-square, f for ANOVA, f² for the linear model. Give a value or `effect_size` instead. Only applies when test is t or t_unequal or two_proportions or two_proportions_unequal or one_proportion or normal_mean or correlation or chisq or anova or linear_model.

effect_size.description: Cohen's conventional small, medium or large effect for this test (pwr's cohen.ES), when there is no estimate from data. A convention, not a measurement, and every answer built on it says so. Only applies when test is t or t_unequal or two_proportions or two_proportions_unequal or one_proportion or normal_mean or correlation or chisq or anova or linear_model.

groups.description: number of groups. Only applies when test is anova_raw.

k.description: number of groups. Only applies when test is anova.

n.description: observations per group (pairs, for paired; the sample, for one-sample and correlation). Only applies when test is t or two_proportions or one_proportion or normal_mean or correlation or anova or t_raw or proportions_raw or anova_raw.

n1.description: observations in the first group. Only applies when test is t_unequal or two_proportions_unequal.

n2.description: observations in the second group. Only applies when test is t_unequal or two_proportions_unequal.

p1.description: the proportion in group 1. Only applies when test is proportions_raw.

p2.description: the proportion in group 2. Only applies when test is proportions_raw.

power.description: 1 − β, the chance of detecting the effect if it is real. No default: the target is yours to choose.

sd.description: the standard deviation, in the same units (of the differences, for paired); R's default is 1. Only applies when test is t_raw.

sig_level.description: α, the type I error rate; R's default.

solve_for.description: the one quantity to solve. Left unset it is the test's sample size (n; n2 for unequal groups, N for chi-square, v for the linear model). `effect` solves the smallest detectable effect.

strict.description: two-sided raw-unit tests: also count rejections in the wrong tail, as R's strict = TRUE. Only applies when test is t_raw or proportions_raw. Advanced.

test.description: which test the experiment will be analyzed with; the power answer belongs to that test and no other. Values: t (t test: one-sample, two-sample or paired, Cohen's d), t_unequal (two-sample t test, unequal group sizes, Cohen's d), two_proportions (two proportions, equal n, Cohen's h), two_proportions_unequal (two proportions, unequal n, Cohen's h), one_proportion (one proportion against a null value, Cohen's h), normal_mean (normal mean, known variance, effect d), correlation (Pearson correlation, r), chisq (chi-square goodness of fit or independence, Cohen's w), anova (balanced one-way ANOVA, Cohen's f), linear_model (linear model F test (multiple regression), Cohen's f²), t_raw (t test in raw units: difference and standard deviation), proportions_raw (two proportions in raw units: p1 and p2), anova_raw (balanced one-way ANOVA in raw units: between- and within-group variance).

type.description: the t test's design. Only applies when test is t or t_raw.

u.description: numerator degrees of freedom: the number of predictors tested. Only applies when test is linear_model.

v.description: denominator degrees of freedom: n − u − 1 for n observations. Only applies when test is linear_model.

within_var.description: variance within groups. Only applies when test is anova_raw.

name: calculate_power

powerCurve.description: power against the sample size, every other quantity held

rCall.description: the R call that reproduces the answer

values.description: every quantity of the test, the solved one included, by R's name

warnings.description: R's own warnings for this solve, verbatim

wholeUnits.description: the sample size rounded up to whole units and the power that whole number gives
